A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and appended material support comparison, including matching results across substantial reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical bounds, proofs, and mathematical illustrations, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: Section 12 reports original accuracy and runtime experiments on MNIST, Forest CoverType, and CLIP embeddings of CIFAR10. Figures 4–9 show experimental outcomes, including sensitivity studies and baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces v1's fine geometric buckets and rounded weights with powers-of-two buckets and a new coordinate transformation that encodes weights in Gaussian or Laplacian KDE queries. The bucket count changes from Θ(log(n/ε)/ε) to Θ(log(n/ε)), with revised error handling. Algorithm 3 also changes its written threshold from τ=mε^3/C to τ=C/(mε^3). The noisy power-iteration procedure itself is retained.

E1.justification: v1 contains no empirical dataset coverage. v2 introduces evaluations of matrix-vector products and top-eigenvalue approximation using MNIST, Forest CoverType, and CLIP embeddings of CIFAR10, principally with the Exponential kernel. These are new linear-algebra evaluations on three represented data domains.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's theoretical comparisons, v2 adds evaluated comparators: Nyström approximation in Section 12.3 and Figure 7, exact matrix-vector computation in Section 12.4 and Figure 8, and the BIMW21 Gaussian matrix-vector method in Section 12.5's query-count and implementation comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces experimental protocols absent from v1: main sample sizes of 1,000 MNIST, 10,000 CoverType, and 500 CLIP points; Exponential-kernel bandwidth targeting mean kernel value 0.001; relative-error metrics; and reference eigenvalues obtained by exact power iteration to convergence. Additional protocols vary bandwidth, iteration count, and dataset size, including timing studies at 10,000–30,000 points.

E4.justification: Section 12 adds empirical sensitivity analyses of eigenvalue error versus matrix-vector precision, convergence versus iteration count, and sensitivity to kernel bandwidth (Figures 4–6 and 9). Figure 8 examines when approximation becomes faster than exact computation as size and precision vary. These practical analyses have no empirical counterparts in v1.

E5.justification: v2 Section 12.1 introduces systematic repeated-run reporting: all experiments are stated to run independently at least 20 times, with one standard deviation shaded in plots. v1 has no empirical repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. This establishes a new reporting practice across the added experimental section.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive concrete results, including approximately linear eigenvalue-error scaling in Figures 4 and 6 and noise-limited convergence in Figure 5. Section 12.4 and Figure 8 report MNIST matrix-vector speedups at ε=0.1 of approximately 1.5 times at n=10,000 and over four times at n=30,000 versus exact computation. These are newly reported outcomes; v1 supplies no empirical values for a before-and-after performance comparison.

T1.justification: v2 adds transformation Lemma 7.1 and substantially revises the matrix-vector proof and stated ε dependence. The mixed-sign lower bounds also change mathematically: Theorem 2.6 and v2 Theorem 10.2 use a modified matrix with exp(-||x_i+x_j||_2^2) off-diagonal entries and unit diagonal, replacing v1's ordinary Gaussian construction. The reduction changes from A union -B to A union B and explicitly bounds within-set interactions.

C1.justification: v1 claims its improved matrix-vector algorithm for any kernel satisfying the KDE assumption; v2 restricts the new improvement to Gaussian and Laplacian kernels and uses BIMW21 for Exponential and Rational Quadratic kernels. The stated Gaussian eigenvalue runtime improves from ε^{-(3+2p)} to ε^{-(3+p)} dependence. Mixed-sign hardness is redefined for the modified matrix family, and empirical corroboration becomes an additional contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of practical error floors, the suitability of linear precision scaling, and Nyström's limitations for high-accuracy eigenvalue estimation. Section 12.4 explains size-versus-accuracy tradeoffs and qualifies timing conclusions by application, hardware, and KDE implementation. Sections 6 and 10 also make the revised kernel applicability and hardness boundaries explicit.

D1.justification: v2 adds an empirical implementation description absent from v1: Python 3.9.7, Numba, an M1 MacBook Pro with 32 GB RAM, random-sampling KDE with ceil(1/ε^2) samples, and a practical BIMW21 matrix-vector implementation using groups differing by 1+ε. Section 12.3 identifies scikit-learn's Nyström implementation. These materially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds practical KDE and Nyström literature, including KAP22, GM16, and WS00, together with dataset and software citations. The discussion extends positioning against additive-error methods, while the central comparison with BIMW21 and most of the theoretical literature remain. This is a focused expansion supporting the new experiments.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative around Gaussian-specific main results and a consolidated technical overview in Section 4. Open questions move from v1 Section 9 to v2 Section 5; general-kernel discussion and proofs appear in appendix Sections 6–11, followed by empirical Section 12. The introduction and algorithm explanations are extensively revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven figures containing experimental plots and computational-cost comparisons (Figures 4–10). Table 1 gains an improvement-factor column and Gaussian-specific presentation. Table 2 removes two summary rows, whose revised theorems remain in Section 10. Existing figures and Table 3 are relocated, and Algorithm 1's displayed procedure is substantially rewritten.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the support and delimitation of its claims. The revised mixed-sign construction explicitly handles within-set interactions missing from v1's argument, while the new weighted-KDE method has a clearer kernel-specific basis. Repeated-run experiments add useful evidence about accuracy, convergence, and practical runtime tradeoffs. Narrower applicability is a substantive tradeoff, but makes the claims more precise. Runtime statements and pseudocode still need reconciliation, including Lemma 7.4's stated exponent versus its proof; these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains.
